solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Snug in little tunic

indicators.note: in places the room's word inside the word for a small amount

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a snug is a small cosy room in a pub, i.e. a bar

explanation.surface: Someone cosily wrapped up in a small tunic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snug' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: a snug is a small private room in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, as worn by heralds or knights over armour.

clue.text: A mostly shy beginner in band is drumming

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to shy is to throw

indicators.note: beginner in means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A timid newcomer in a group is playing the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is the verb, to throw, not timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Athrob means throbbing or pulsating, like a beating drum.

clue.text: End of hostilities from division cities sorted out

parts.note: an arm is a division or branch of an organisation

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: Wars ended by cities resolving their differences.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, the agreed halt to fighting.

clue.text: Criminal provides name shown to be false

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent or corrupted

explanation.surface: A crook gives a name that turns out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A disproven claim has been demonstrated to be untrue.

clue.text: High-ranking Italian with Spanish help going west

parts.note: con is the Spanish word for with

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means the word is read right to left

parts.note: an asset is something that helps, a resource

explanation.surface: A senior Italian figure getting assistance from Spain as things decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' also suggests things failing, but here it reverses ASSET to TESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman of noble rank.

clue.text: Perhaps pine after one's broken award

indicators.note: broken means the award word is split open with the other letter inserted

parts.note: to confer is to award
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a prize after breaking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine after' reads as yearning, but 'pine' is a tree and 'after' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is one example of a cone-bearing tree, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Illustrious inventor's left to go north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means moving up, nearer the top of the word

parts.note: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite

explanation.surface: A famous inventor departs for the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean distinguished or illustrious in character or rank.

clue.text: Hard to carry on lifting for some time

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to cope is to carry on despite difficulty
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is hard to keep lifting weights for long.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period, an era.

clue.text: Guarantee cruise at sea ends in Turkey

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
ends in means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A sea cruise finishing in Turkey comes with a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: Security is a pledge or collateral given as a guarantee.

clue.text: Interrupts that man in church, not a good thing

indicators.note: in puts the pronoun inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him refers to that man
a sin is a wrong, not a good thing

explanation.surface: A man in church doing something bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime in is to break into a conversation with a remark, to interject.

clue.text: Horse riding clubs acquired by sibling

indicators.note: acquired by means the sibling word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a sibling
riding on a horse, so on
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A horse used by a brother for riding to a golf or social club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is a wild or half-tamed horse of the American West.

clue.text: Cat runs after short time to exercise

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the other two pieces

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a short time
to exercise a right is to use it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cat sprinting after a brief workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept or valued for catching mice.

clue.text: Leaving Religious Education out of courses to update students

indicators.note: leaving something out means omitting it from the word

parts.note: taken from refresher courses, which bring knowledge up to date
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: Skipping the RE part of training courses meant to keep students current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' with 'out of' signals the omission. FRESHERS is British for first-year university students.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshers are new university students in their first year, a British term.

clue.text: Maybe cockroach one time found in tavern drunk with beer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A cockroach discovered in a pub where beer has been spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' and 'with' just gather I, T, TAVERN and BEER into one pool for 'drunk' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is one example of an animal lacking a backbone, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Moving book about Scottish island lake

indicators.note: about means the book word is turned round

parts.note: a tome is a large book
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A touching book about a Scottish island and its loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving and emotional both describe something that stirs the feelings.

clue.text: To set up mother with acting part is hassle

parts.note: to rig is to set up, as with equipment
ma is mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Getting your mother a part in a play is a bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious procedure, a hassle.

clue.text: Whizz round Cologne with a primitive mode of transport

indicators.note: whizzing round suggests the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Speeding round a German city in an old-fashioned vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout boat hollowed from a tree trunk is among the earliest kinds of watercraft.

clue.text: Firm with hideous monster, no good to behave aggressively

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: hideous suggests the letters are deformed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A company with an ugly monster turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act in an overly forceful or pushy manner toward someone.

clue.text: Very sweet lady disheartened, stuck under collapsed crate

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck under places the second piece below the first
collapsed suggests the letters fall into a new order
disheartened means the middle letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: A sweet lady, downcast and trapped beneath a fallen crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacly describes something like syrup, cloyingly sweet.

clue.text: Almost gag, about to bring up a food crop

indicators.note: almost means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a quip is a joke, a gag

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means reading the word upward

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Nearly retching, about to vomit a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests vomiting after 'gag', but here it signals an upward reading in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinoa is an Andean plant grown for its edible seeds.

clue.text: Officer Bill overwhelmed by great praise

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the officer and bill are swallowed inside the word for great

parts.note: ace means excellent, great
Col is short for Colonel, an officer
ad is short for advertisement, a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A soldier and a man named Bill receive lavish praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of high praise.

clue.text: Start running group

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A running club starting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning of something.

clue.text: Musical people like Mary Poppins limitlessly

indicators.note: limitlessly means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Mary Poppins is a fictional nanny

explanation.surface: A musical full of Mary Poppins types, without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Poppins suggests one musical, but the answer is another.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage show about the orphan girl Little Orphan Annie is a Broadway musical.

clue.text: Craftsman's son making section for basilica, Russia

indicators.note: section for means a run of letters lifted from the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A builder's son producing part of a Russian basilica.
explanation.walkthrough: The craftsman is Daedalus, the mythical inventor who built wings for himself and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the flyer who soared too near the sun was the son of the master craftsman Daedalus.

clue.text: Club hosts second concert

indicators.note: hosts means the club word holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a union is an association, a club

explanation.surface: A club putting on a second concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is not a performance here but its sense of agreement, as in 'acting in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert can mean agreement or harmony, the same sense as acting together as one.

clue.text: Do start puzzle

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them
to found something is to start it

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to bewilder or perplex someone, so to puzzle them.

clue.text: Tough article stuck in meadow track

indicators.note: stuck in means the article is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
RY is short for railway, a track
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Something tough wedged in a field path.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery describes something hard and chewy, like tough meat.

clue.text: Room of Spooner's small place

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: Spooner's tiny lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of WEE LAY gives LEE WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, latitude or freedom of action.
